nodes.description: External function verify_relay_staker_address(int8,uint256) that accepts arbitrary callers and emits RelayAddressVerified without any caller authorization or validation.
msg.sender, attacker-controllable caller address that is cast to uint160 and written into the RelayAddressVerified event, allowing anyone to forge a relay address verification.

Unauthenticated event emission of RelayAddressVerified(uint160(msg.sender), workchain_id, address_body); the lack of access control lets any external account create trusted-looking verification records.
Input parameter workchain_id (int8) supplied by the caller and forwarded into the emitted RelayAddressVerified event with no validation.
Input parameter address_body (uint256) supplied by the caller and forwarded into the emitted RelayAddressVerified event with no validation.

edges.reason: msg.sender is cast to uint160 and used as the eth_addr field of the RelayAddressVerified event, so an arbitrary caller controls the identity that gets recorded as a verified relay address.
The external function execute path reaches the emit with no caller check (no owner, role or require on msg.sender), so any account can trigger the privileged verification event.
Caller-supplied workchain_id parameter flows unchanged into the RelayAddressVerified event payload.
Caller-supplied address_body parameter flows unchanged into the RelayAddressVerified event payload.

normalization_plan.reason: workchain_id is only a transient input of verify_relay_staker_address and carries no independent identity, so it should be folded into the enclosing function node.
address_body is only a transient input of verify_relay_staker_address and carries no independent identity, so it should be folded into the enclosing function node.
